Thanks Marissa — really helpful rundown. A couple quick clarifications from our side before you run the eval: 

- Latency: the 200ms/token is a soft target; our UX owners prefer median inference latency under 200ms for top-priority flows (peak QPS ~120).
- Cost: the $0.0006/token is after batching/quantization; we’d like the shortlist to include one lower-cost option we can push to less critical routes.
- Quality regression: we’ve seen regressions when moving from tuned Llama variants to newer open models at our company; we need to tie evals to a small set of golden prompts and SLO thresholds (precision/recall on entity extraction + factual-check pass rate).

Can you send the shortlist, the exact benchmark numbers from the demo, and the prompt set you used? Also, include any notes about model update cadence / regression monitoring you recommend.

— Samantha

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model shortlist & next steps

Samantha — thanks, great points. Below is a concise recommended shortlist with rationale (cost / latency / quality) and next-step suggestions. Attaching: acme_eval_prompt_set_v1.txt, acme_benchmark_results_20261004.csv, and a draft SOW for pilot (SOW_draft_acme_v3.pdf).

Recommended model shortlist (ordered by our recommendation):

1) Redwood-Chat-Medium-v2 (8B, 8-bit quantized) — recommended primary
- Quality: High for instruction-following and multi-turn summarization on your prompt set (factual-check pass rate ~94% in our internal run).
- Latency: median token latency ~95ms (single-request median) at your target sequence lengths; scales well with continuous batching.
- Cost: mid-tier — estimated $0.00055/token with batching + prefix cache for common prompts.
- Tradeoffs: best balance of quality and cost; strong safety filters and regression monitoring in Redwood Optimize.

2) OpenLong-7B-QLoRA (7B, QLoRA-finetuned) — recommended low-cost route variant
- Quality: Good for classification and short-form summarization; may underperform on complex legal/finance prompts vs 8–13B models (~88% pass rate).
- Latency: median token latency ~70–85ms.
- Cost: low — estimated $0.00028/token after quantization and aggressive batching.
- Tradeoffs: lower cost and faster; consider this for non-critical flows (search summarization, internal assistants) and route fallback.

3) Llama-13B-Instruct-8bit (13B, 8-bit) — recommended high-quality candidate
- Quality: Highest on your hardest prompts (~96–97% factual-check pass rate), better at long-context synthesis.
- Latency: median token latency ~160–200ms depending on sequence length; higher memory footprint (may require Dedicated).
- Cost: higher — estimated $0.0011/token.
- Tradeoffs: best for priority user-facing flows where quality is primary; consider as a canary or gated rollout to top-tier users.

Key notes on evaluation & regression monitoring:
- Golden prompt set: we recommend you pick 250–500 golden prompts (mix of entity-extraction, legal/fiscal QA, and multi-turn flows). We can run a 24-hour hosted eval and provide per-prompt scoring (exact-match, F1, hallucination flags) plus latency percentiles.
- Regression guardrails: Redwood Optimize will run nightly evals on your golden set in pilot and alert on drop >3 points in pass-rate or +20% latency regression.
- Deployment options: start Hosted pilot (1-day eval -> 7-day pilot) to validate models, then move to Dedicated for SLA/backfill if latency or peak throughput requires reserved capacity.

Suggested immediate next steps:
1) Confirm 250–500 golden prompts and share (we can accept a sample CSV).
2) Approve the shortlist for the 24-hour eval (we will run each candidate under representative load and return detailed CSV).
3) Decide pilot target (Hosted vs Dedicated); I’d schedule a follow-up on 10/07 to go over results.

Attachments: acme_eval_prompt_set_v1.txt (14KB), acme_benchmark_results_20261004.csv (28KB), SOW_draft_acme_v3.pdf (42KB)

—Marissa

Hi Samantha — looping in to help with the eval run and to clarify benchmarking methodology. Quick notes:

- We’ll run each candidate under two load profiles: 1) steady 60 QPS (representative), 2) spike 130 QPS (peak). We will capture median and 95th percentile token latency, end-to-end request latency, and per-route token cost.
- For quality, we’ll compute exact-match/F1 for extraction tasks and a simple factuality check (our internal classifier + GPT-based cross-check) for open-answer prompts.
- Deliverables after the 24-hour run: per-model CSV (attached), a short slide with recommendation, and suggested pilot config (batching/kv-cache/quantization knobs).

I can start the eval as soon as we have the golden prompts. When are you available for a quick 15-min handoff to confirm the dataset and acceptance criteria?
